## TL;DR

The sign-in and session-expiry flows now pass the headless QA suites at 375, 768 and 1280 px. The branch carries the login fixes from earlier WIP commits, plus two fixes made in this session. The first is a test-fixture gap that broke the #1249 notifications QA test once the new session-expiry redirect landed. The second is a unit test that could not see the redirect because `api()` checked `window`, which does not exist in the node test environment. The scoped check result is recorded at the end of this draft.

## Work and rationale

The branch already held the core changes from earlier WIP commits:

- `src/ui-app/src/api.ts`: a 401 whose body is the server's session-gate reply (`Authentication required`) now sends the visitor to `/login?expired=1&redirect=<here>`. The caller still gets its `ApiError`. Other 401s, such as a provider rejecting a key, are left alone. The router guard only runs on client navigation, so without this an expired session left the dashboard up with failing requests.
- `src/ui-app/src/views/LoginView.vue`: the expired-session message, a "Use a different email" action that clears the code step's error and half-typed code, 44px tap targets on the resend and change-email links, a visible `:focus-visible` ring on login inputs, spinners on Verify and Create Admin, and clearing the resend interval on unmount.
- Tests: `login-session-flows-qa-browser.test.ts` (headless WebKit, three widths), `login-view-session-flows.test.ts`, and `api-session-expiry.test.ts`.

In this session I changed two things:

1. `api()` now redirects through the global `location` instead of `window.location`. In the browser these are the same object. In the node test environment `window` is undefined, so the early return fired and the unit test saw no redirect. The change is one line, and the unit test passes through `bun run test`.
2. `src/ui-app/tests/notifications-settings-qa-browser.test.ts` (#1249) now answers `GET /api/auth/users` from a fixture. The failure came from my redirect. The notifications tab's fixture says `authEnabled: true` and `authenticated: true`, but the in-process fixture server runs with auth off. The admin account panel loads alongside the tab and reached `requireAdmin`, which returned 401 `Authentication required`. The new redirect treated that as an expired session and navigated away. The navigation aborted in-flight requests, and WebKit reported them as uncaught page errors. The test's header already says every fetch from the tab is answered from fixtures, so I added the missing route. I did not weaken the redirect or the test's no-page-errors assertion.

No separate lock-screen surface exists in `src/ui-app`. The sign-in flow is the one I covered. The shot declarations (`auth:login` and `auth:otp`) resolve to fixtures in `src/core/shot-fixtures.ts`.

## Approaches tried

- To isolate the notifications failure, I reverted `api.ts` and `LoginView.vue` to main's versions and rebuilt the UI. All 13 tests passed. Restoring the branch's versions brought back the 12 failures.
- To confirm the redirect was the cause, I temporarily made `redirectToSignIn` a no-op and rebuilt. All 13 passed again.
- To find which request produced the 401, I temporarily logged passthrough statuses in the notifications test. That showed `GET /api/auth/users` as the only 401. I reverted the logging before any real change.
- I also probed the in-process fixture server directly with a scratch script outside the repo. Its `/api/models`, `/api/config/raw`, `/api/remote-validation/status` and `/api/config` all returned 200, so the failure was not in those routes.

Scoped check: `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` exited 0. Remote validation on the thinkpad runner passed in 951s, the rendered contrast audit passed, and the UI smoke test passed.

Rejected options: making the redirect skip when auth is off. That needs the client to know the server's auth state, and the fixture contradicts itself on that point. The test fixture gap was the smaller and more accurate fix.

## Challenges and blockers

- An early `build:ui` run failed on a type error that my own temporary debug line introduced (`text()` does not exist on the route response). It was reverted.
- The first runs used whatever `dist` build existed, so I rebuilt from the exact tree under test before trusting any result.
- Bare `bunx vitest run` fails to parse `.vue` imports in several suites with "install @vitejs/plugin-vue". The project wrapper (`bun run test`) handles them. The repo's AGENTS.md says to use the wrapper, and I did.
- Server-side, `requireAdmin` in `src/server/routes/auth.ts` returns 401 `Authentication required` whenever auth is disabled, because `getCurrentUser` returns null. The client gates these calls on `auth.authEnabled`, so no real auth-off path reaches them today. I did not change that server behaviour. It is worth a follow-up task.
- Human proof is not covered here. I did not test on a real device, and no real credentials were used. Everything used dev-login or fixture data.

## Key learnings

- A shared client helper that reacts to a status code (here, a 401 redirect) can change the behaviour of every test that leaves a route unanswered. Before adding such a helper, list every fetch the tabs under test make and answer each one from fixtures.
- A fixture that claims auth is on while the server runs with auth off produces 401s that look like real expired sessions. Keep fixture flags consistent with the server being served.
- A `window` guard in a helper also needs `location` to be readable in the test environment. Use the global `location` for these redirects.
- Isolate a failure by reverting one side at a time, rebuilding each time. That settled the cause in three builds.
